packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

packet-22 - isolated first reading (unverified image reading)
Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview, face A)
- Small parchment fragment (~9 x 15 cm by the scale), assembled from several horizontal strips mounted together; strips are misaligned, with tears/folds between them. A large grey rectangle masks the upper left (~9 x 5.5 cm) - image redaction, not text.
- The visible text lies in the right part: a narrow text column (or two narrow column segments separated by a vertical tear/join at roughly mid-strip). Only the right ~40% of the fragment carries legible script on this face; the left part is blank/abraded parchment with faint offset (red) traces.
- Many red rubric lines of the form "De ... x(?) q(uestio?) N" interspersed with short brown-ink lines; a red vertical bracket line and red dotted/dashed vertical line run down the left edge of the text block; one blue mark (paragraph sign?) visible mid-left of the column. Pattern looks like a list/index of headings with references (tentative: a table of contents or index), but this is interpretation.
- Heavy abrasion, staining, creasing; brown-ink lines largely faded.

SUMMARY OF SELECTION AND LIMITATIONS
- All six images viewed: two overviews (001 face A, 004 face B) and four native tiles (002, 003 face A; 005, 006 face B), plus 10 crops in rscratch/packet-22/. No image limit reached.
- Content observed: on both faces a single narrow text block with frequent red rubric lines of the shape "De <topic> [sign like x with superscript stroke] .q. <roman numeral>" (numerals seen: xl, xii/xu, xl..iii, xxxiii, xxxiiii, xxxv, xxxvi?), separated by short brown-ink lines of running text, with red brackets, red dotted guide lines and blue paragraph marks. This looks like a list of headings with question references (tentative: index/table, or headings inside a running text) - an interpretation only.
- Most secure readings: "De temptat(i)o(n)e x .q. xii/xu" (002.11); "-catio(n)e x .q. xl" (002.02); marginal "De natiuitate / saluatoris / .q. xxxv(?)" (005 M.1-3); "(con)cepte .q. xxxiiii(?)" (005.12); "...iatione p(ri)uile|galib(us) / i(n)su(?) obs(er)uat(ur) / .q. ..." (006.19-21); brown "illo aliud(?)" (005.10), "..s(an)c(t)ificat(ur)(?)" (005.13), "alia" (006.14).
- Brown running text is mostly abraded; no span of ten connected legible lines exists on either face - the leaf condition (washed, stained, strip-cut, creased) not effort limits this. Unread: brown lines 002.04-07, 002.12-15, 003.13-15, 005.06-09, 005.15-18 left halves, 006.10-11, 006.15-18, 006.22-23.
- Strips are misaligned; the vertical tear splits each line into left/right segments and I assumed each line continues across the tear at the same height - not certain for every line. Face B column order relative to face A not determined.
- Suggest multispectral/UV imaging for the brown-ink lines; red rubrics are the best anchors.
- Exposure / extra steps: none. I read only PROMPT.md, the six packet images, and my own crops. The pencil note "Stams(?) StA" is visible on the leaf; I report it as text only and drew no identification from it.
